cases.name: >= row with a negative right-hand side, binding
cases.why: the engine negates the row to normalise it; the dual must follow the ORIGINAL row

cases.name: <= row with a negative right-hand side, binding
cases.why: maximise x with y - x <= -2; the row binds only through the bound on x, so its price is zero while the bound carries the value

cases.name: = row with a negative right-hand side
cases.why: the equality dual must keep the sign of the row as written

cases.name: blend shape: <= spec row, component floor shifts rhs negative
cases.why: the rhs is 0 as written and -A*lo after the shift, so the engine flips a row the caller never flipped

cases.name: blend shape: >= spec row, component floor shifts rhs negative
cases.why: the same spec written as a minimum

cases.name: redundant equality rows
cases.why: an artificial stays basic at zero after phase one

cases.name: degenerate vertex, three rows through one point
cases.why: the optimum sits on three constraints in two dimensions, so the duals are an interval

cases.name: maximise, textbook
cases.why: Hillier and Lieberman Wyndor shape: x=2, y=6, z=36, duals 0, 1.5, 1

cases.name: maximise with a >= row
cases.why: a binding upper bound and a slack >= row

cases.name: infeasible through bounds
cases.why: a row that no value inside the bounds can meet

cases.name: infeasible by a twentieth
cases.why: phase one ends with 0.05 left in its artificials; a loose feasibility test calls this solvable

cases.name: infeasible by a millionth
cases.why: the smallest miss the engine is asked to see, ten times its 1e-7 feasibility threshold

cases.name: bounded only by an upper bound
cases.why: a bound, not a row, stops the objective

cases.name: fuzz-found: an equality row broken at the returned optimum
cases.why: the engine returned x = (0, 3, 7, 9), where the equality row reads -33 against -3

cases.name: fuzz-found: a <= row broken at the returned optimum
cases.why: found by the same 100k fuzz; an artificial left basic at zero after phase one goes positive in phase two

cases.name: false unbounded: a bounded problem with a degenerate >= row
cases.why: x + y <= 2 with y >= 2 pins x = 0; the engine reported unbounded

cases.name: lower bounds lift the origin
cases.why: the bound already satisfies the row, which prices at zero

provenance.method: exact rational vertex enumeration; shadow prices as exact one-sided derivatives by re-solve
provenance.published: none: an LP optimum is a mathematical fact of the problem, so no literature value is needed or claimed
